title: Firewalls
intro: The core policy-routes each seat range to its firewall. Here you see which firewall each range should take, which it takes now, and how the firewalls are.
splitIntro: Cut a network into equal ranges and share them out over the firewalls in turn: the first range goes to the first firewall, the second to the second, and so on. Ranges planned already stay as they are.
splitSizeHelp: The prefix length of each range, for example 24 for one range per third octet.
splitNameHelp: Optional. The ranges are numbered after it.
splitTooMany: That makes more than 256 ranges: pick a larger range size.
none: No firewalls yet. Give the firewalls the role Firewall in the inventory, then plan their ranges here.
noRangesEdit: No ranges planned yet. Add each seat range the core routes to a firewall.
unread: The monitoring source can't be read right now: the ranges show their planned firewall.
moved_one: {{count}} range is not on its planned firewall
moved_other: {{count}} ranges are not on their planned firewall
name: Name
lineHelp: The firewall the core routes this range to.
importHelp: Reads the NetBox prefixes that have the custom field floorbit_firewalls (their firewalls, in order). Each import replaces the last; ranges planned here stay.
fromPluginHelp: Change it in {{plugin}} and import again.
noMonitoring: No monitoring source is set up, so the ranges show their planned firewall. An admin adds LibreNMS (or another monitoring plugin) under Settings.
switchesHelp: Optional. Seats behind these switches with an address outside their ranges show under Problems: a wrong port, a wrong VLAN or a router of their own. Left empty, each switch's range is the one most of its seats are in.
splitFallback: Each range falls back to the next firewall while its own is down
fallbackHelp: Optional. Only if the core moves the range while its firewall is down, in this order. Left empty, the range is down with its firewall.
